summary.text: A geologic hazard is a harmful geologic condition, from a small feature to a huge landslide, that can cause widespread damage and loss of life and property.
Human choices such as careless siting of buildings or drilling through overpressured zones can create serious risk, so understanding hazards' causes is key to prevention.
Volcanism can matter on a global scale: large volcanic provinces from ancient flood basalt eruptions have been connected to five mass extinctions.

facts.label: Flood basalt episodes
facts.value: Eleven in the past 250 million years

facts.label: Mass extinctions linked
facts.value: Five, tied to large igneous provinces

facts.label: Slope fixes
facts.value: Retaining walls, soil nails, tiebacks and anchors

facts.label: Shore protection
facts.value: Revetments and riprap against scour and erosion

items.prompt: A town wants to stop a steep hillside from sliding onto homes below it. Which fix is a standard choice?

options.label: A retaining wall held with soil anchors
Extra fill piled along the hilltop
Heavy watering to bind the loose soil
Clearing all plants off the slope

items.explain: Retaining walls, using methods such as soil nails, tiebacks or soil anchors, improve the stability of sloping ground.

items.prompt: In high mountains, an avalanche crashes into a lake. What can that set off?

options.label: A harmless splash that settles within an hour
A debris flow whose effects reach far away
A small earthquake felt only at the lake
A sudden freeze across the lake's surface

items.explain: Such chain events can turn into a debris flow, with consequences potentially hundreds of miles away.

items.prompt: A developer puts homes on a site without studying its ground conditions, and the land later fails. What does this show?

options.label: Hazards only come from natural processes
Ground failure happens only in mountains
Careless siting of buildings can set off hazards
Building codes make all ground safe

items.explain: Hazards are sometimes set off by placing developments where the local conditions were not taken into account.

items.prompt: Why do scientists suspect giant ancient volcanic outpourings could change Earth's climate?

options.label: Their lava reflected sunlight for millions of years
Their ash fell only into the deep oceans
They happened only during ice ages
Many line up in time with global warming

items.explain: Six of eleven known provinces coincide with periods of global warming and low ocean oxygen, suggesting volcanic CO₂ can affect climate.

items.prompt: A growing city must choose where new neighbourhoods can safely go. What helps most directly?

options.label: Mapping hazards from the ground or by remote sensing
Building wherever land is cheapest first
Waiting to see where damage happens
Copying another city's street plan

items.explain: Mapping geohazards with conventional or remote sensing methods helps identify areas suitable for urban development.

items.prompt: A council wants a rule-based way to cut hazard risk rather than an engineering project. What fits?

options.label: Injecting grout into the weak soil
Banning new building in risky zones
Lining the riverbanks with riprap
Setting homes on deep foundations

items.explain: Planning measures include regulations that prohibit development near hazard-prone areas, along with building codes.
